newsitem.title: FRANCE: Minister talks to Brussels on French film firm SFP.
newsitem.headline: Minister talks to Brussels on French film firm SFP.

text.p: French Culture Minister Philippe Douste-Blazy says he is talking to European Commission officials in Brussels over the future of loss-making French state film production firm Societe Francaise de Production (SFP), which is earmarked for privatisation.
"I am renegotiating with Brussels... in no case will there be a compartmentalised sale," he said at the opening of the MIP television trade fair in Cannes on Friday.
Douste-Blazy said he would do all he could to avoid a liquidation of SFP.
A source close to the privatisation procedure said earlier this week that the privatisation tender could be declared null and void as no acceptable offer had been made.

The tender period expires on April 18. Swiss businessman Fabrice Giger, who has made an offer for SFP, is due to meet the SFP works council on Monday, but trade union sources say his offer for SFP is unlikely to be accepted.
An SFP executive told Reuters that cleaning up his company's accounts would require 500 million to 600 million francs.
He said Douste-Blazy could be asking Brussels to be allowed to plough this amount into SFP. But the European Commission is unhappy about France subsidising SFP, he said.
